title: Uniform projective resolution bound for finite perfect quotients
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. For every integer $n\geq1$ put $P_n=A/I^n$, using the ideal powers and quotients of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Suppose every $P_n$ is finite as a set and its degree-zero complex is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. There is an integer $r\geq0$, independent of $n$, such that every $P_n$ has a resolution by finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module] concentrated in cochain degrees $[-r,0]$. Equivalently, for the same $r$, for every $n\geq1$ and every $A$-module $M$, the derived tensor $P_n\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ has cohomology only in degrees $[-r,0]$; here derived tensor is computed by tensoring a projective resolution of $P_n$ with $M$, so $H^{-i}=\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(P_n,M)$ for $i\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. The zero quotient is allowed.

source.place: Tag 090V, proposition-Auslander-Buchsbaum: applied to the nonzero finite-length localizations of the perfect quotients. The common-bound conclusion is an agent assembly, not the literal statement of 090V.

proof.text: For each quotient use the K-projective bounded-model argument to obtain finite projective dimension. This uses only perfectness and does not require positive-tail cancellation.

Let T be the maximal ideals containing I. The map m↦m/I, realized as m.map(A→A/I), embeds T into the subsets of A/I: contraction recovers m since I≤m. Since A/I is finite, T is finite. Each R=A_m is Noetherian local. Its depth is finite because depth(R)≤dim Supp(R)=dim(R), and a Noetherian local ring has finite Krull dimension. Choose a natural r bounding the depth of every such R, using the maximum of a finite range (including the empty-range case).

Localize P_n=A/I^n at a maximal ideal m. Mathlib localizedModule_hasProjectiveDimensionLE preserves the finite bound from the first step. If the localization is nonzero, the support-annihilator criterion gives I^n≤m. Primality implies I≤m, so m∈T. Finite generation survives localization. Auslander–Buchsbaum gives pd((P_n)_m)+depth((P_n)_m)=depth(A_m)≤r, hence pd((P_n)_m)≤r. If it is zero, it has projective dimension at most r without further assumptions. Use the categorical Auslander–Buchsbaum equality directly in WithBot ℕ∞; nonnegativity of module depth and projectiveDimension_le_iff give the desired Ext bound without a natural-number projective-dimension wrapper or bounded-resolution comparison.
Each quotient is cyclic, hence finitely generated. The maximal-localization criterion turns the preceding local bound into HasProjectiveDimensionLE P_n r globally.

Construct a resolution by finite projectives with bound r using the new finite-presentation induction lemma. This handles r=0 and zero quotients, and needs neither a chosen initial finite resolution nor its syzygy-shortening criterion.

Tensor such a resolution with an arbitrary module. ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj computes Tor as its homology; tensor sends zero terms to zero, so Tor vanishes above r. Conversely, the finite-module Tor-bound criterion gives the global projective-dimension bound at the prescribed r. Apply the bounded finite-projective-resolution constructor independently for every positive n. Thus the two uniform conditions are equivalent at the same r.

split_report.summary: Proved a common bound r given by the length of a finite projective resolution of A/I, using the elementary depth-zero calculation for finite A/I at supported maximal ideals, the general Auslander–Buchsbaum formula and the Mathlib local-global Ext-bound criterion. Made tensor explicitly derived, removed the unrelated completed sheaf datum from the algebraic statement, and wrote out perfect-model cancellation, localization, shortening and the converse Tor formulation. Two genuinely general ingredients are new: one statement-only formula and one Mathlib leaf.
